final_answer:
Endurance training elicited a broad, systemic, and partly coordinated multi-omic response across organs rather than a muscle-only response. The provided significant differential-result table contained 35,441 unique tissue-assay regulated feature records, representing 22,606 unique feature keys across 20 tissues and 9 assays. Liver had the largest regulated-feature inventory (5,929 unique feature keys), followed by adrenal (4,605), subcutaneous white adipose (3,115), heart (3,079), gastrocnemius skeletal muscle (2,817), brown adipose (2,774), colon (2,574), and lung (2,143). Timewise contrast evidence was present at all durations and was largest at 8 weeks (30,888 nominally timewise-significant rows), indicating persistent and expanding remodeling over training.

The tissues with the most similar changes were the two skeletal muscles, gastrocnemius (SKM-GN) and vastus lateralis (SKM-VL). They ranked first in the combined similarity analysis, with mean feature-set Jaccard similarity of 0.153 across 3 shared assays and a weighted signed temporal Spearman correlation of 0.713 across 1,896 matched sex-time effect values. This makes them the strongest example of coordinated organ-level training response in the dataset.

The next strongest coordinated pair was cortex and hippocampus, with weighted temporal Spearman correlation of 0.661 and mean sign agreement of 0.692 across 3 shared assays, although their absolute shared feature count was smaller. Other notable multi-assay similarities included kidney-spleen, brown adipose-lung, kidney-lung, liver-gastrocnemius, heart-gastrocnemius, and heart-liver. Set-overlap alone highlighted adrenal-spleen as the highest feature-identity overlap pair, but its signed temporal coordination was weaker than the skeletal-muscle and cortex-hippocampus pairs.

Overall, endurance training produces coordinated molecular remodeling across many organs, with the clearest concordance within related tissue systems: skeletal muscles show the strongest shared training trajectory, brain regions also respond coherently, and several cardiometabolic/immune-visceral tissue pairs show moderate shared programs. Because the input table contains only precomputed significant features and assay coverage differs by tissue, these rankings should be interpreted as comparative similarity of regulated molecular signatures, not as causal organ-to-organ signaling evidence.

grader_notes: The agent successfully handled data parsing, FDR filtering, de-duplication, and per-assay set similarity. Coverage gaps were explicitly addressed, and cross-assay aggregation was principled. The biological interpretation was present but lacked explicit citations to MoTrPAC or other specific references in the text, making it not fully meet the A level for criterion 7.

criterion_1.reason: Correctly identified assay and tissue fields, iterated over all 9 omes, and reported per-tissue unique feature counts and assay coverage.

criterion_2.reason: Used the pre-existing training_q < 0.05 FDR threshold consistently across all assays without applying additional filters.

criterion_3.reason: De-duplicated features by feature_key within each (tissue, assay) by dropping duplicates before building sets.

criterion_4.reason: Computed tissue × tissue similarity per assay using well-defined Jaccard and overlap coefficient metrics.

criterion_5.reason: Explicitly handled coverage gaps by requiring both tissues to have data in an assay, reporting shared assay counts, and imposing a minimum of 3 shared assays for ranking.

criterion_6.reason: Aggregated per-assay similarities using mean/median for set overlap and weighted Fisher z-transform for temporal similarity, preventing dominance by a single assay.

criterion_7.reason: Interpretation identified top pairs and provided plausible biological rationale, but did not cite the MoTrPAC main publication or other identifiable exercise-physiology references in-text, and some claims lack source attribution.
